# DESIGN-SOURCED ICP (Ateles): the multi-principal system, phase 1

## Archetype

By design (docs/foundation/, origin/main), Ateles is a multi-principal authority system whose FIRST PHASE is a single operator delegating to many agents. The single-operator case is explicitly named in the design as one case of a general model, not the model's endpoint. Design authority: README.md ('Today it assumes one operator who owns the machine, the keypairs, and the Neotoma instance — the single-principal case of the multi-operator model described below.'); docs/foundation/authority_model.md ('the design is multi-principal in earnest, with real separation of duties, real quorum, and real attenuating delegation... the risk is scale, not applicability'); docs/foundation/multi_tenant.md decision 82 ('Every instance may have one operator or many, whoever hosts it and wherever it is deployed, so multi-operator is a property every instance has and not a consequence of a hosting arrangement').

## Stack

Same substrate as the implementation-derived ICP (claude CLI/Claude Code + MCP, Python, Neotoma, launchd/Docker, SOPS+age, self-provisioned keypairs), on the design's own account NOT rebuilt for multi-operator: README.md states 'the substrate was deliberately built so the single-operator case is not a dead end: agents already carry their own verified identities, capability is already entity-scoped rather than assumed, and high-blast actions already checkpoint to a principal. Multi-operator is an extension of the entity model (more principals, ownership, delegation edges), not a rewrite.'

## Core job to be done

Same five objectives as the implementation-derived ICP's core_jtbd (Operate, Govern, Remember, Extend, Trust the dangerous parts — docs/foundation/charter.md), stated for a system of MULTIPLE human principals rather than one: authority that is explicit, scoped, and revocable BETWEEN humans as well as from a human to an agent; every action attributed to the principal — human or agent — it was taken for; structural checks (quorum, separation of duties) that require distinct human interests to be satisfiable at all; delegation chains and approval matrices across named human roles, not only across agents. Per the charter's purpose statement: Ateles exists 'to let work be initiated, executed, and approved by humans and agents together' (plural humans, not 'a human') 'under authority that is explicit, scoped, and revocable, with every action attributed to the principal it was taken for.'

## Trigger moment

By design, the trigger is not only the solo operator's 'I have become the integration layer' moment (which is P1's trigger) but the moment a solo operator's swarm needs to admit a SECOND accountable human principal — a co-founder, an employee, a contractor with their own scoped authority — and discovers that quorum, separation of duties, and per-human delegation require a distinct principal model the single-operator build does not yet enforce, even though the model to enforce it is already designed (authority_model.md, multi_tenant.md).

## Messaging — good

Speaks to: an operator or team that expects to GROW from one principal to several without a rewrite — the design's own claim that 'multi-operator is an extension of the entity model, not a rewrite' (README.md); wanting quorum and separation-of-duties enforced structurally between distinct humans, not only logged in prose; wanting a system whose identity model (agent entities, principal_binding, acts-as) already anticipates more than one accountable human before that second human exists. This is a forward-looking design claim, not a claim about what a checkout does today — see the reconciliation for where this diverges from present build state.

## Messaging — bad (anti-profile)

NOT a claim that multi-operator is built or usable today — per status.md, P2-P5 have 'nothing built' beyond the identity decision (C9) and the multi_tenant.md section-7 decisions (79-83), which are ruled at the design level but have no runtime reader (status.md P2 row: 'no principal entity has a runtime reader'). Not a claim that Ateles is an enterprise IAM product — authority_model.md is explicit that the design achieves multi-principal governance 'without enterprise-scale machinery (policy administration consoles, role mining, certification campaigns, hierarchy-shaped approval routing); the risk is scale, not applicability.' Not evidence that the implementation-derived ICP (ent_fd64f687e7e1bf5711c6de2b) is wrong about the CURRENT build — it correctly describes P1. The two views diverge specifically on the anti-profile item excluding 'teams or multi-operator organizations,' addressed in the reconciliation analysis.

## Ideal entry point

Per the design (not yet buildable): standing up the P1 substrate as a single operator first — the design's own sequencing states the single-operator case is not a dead end, and P2 is 'an extension of the entity model,' so the entry point for a design-sourced adopter is identical to the implementation-derived ICP's entry point today (Neotoma + identities + capability grants + one daemon), with the multi-operator extension arriving as a later, additive phase rather than a different starting point.

## Summary

DESIGN-SOURCED (not implementation-derived) ICP for Ateles, projected from docs/foundation/ at origin/main — specifically README.md's 'single-principal case of the multi-operator model' framing, docs/foundation/authority_model.md's multi-principal quorum/separation-of-duties decisions (48-50), docs/foundation/multi_tenant.md's decision 82, and docs/foundation/status.md's P1-P5 roadmap table. States who Ateles is FOR by design, including phases that are designed and unbuilt — this is the second, independently-derived view alongside the implementation-derived ent_fd64f687e7e1bf5711c6de2b; see analysis (reconciliation) for where the two agree and disagree. Reviewed by: architect.
